ruling.explanation:
This dispute turns on one question — did the driver reach the Tiong Bahru Plaza pickup point and hold position there for the required five minutes? — and the only evidence that can answer it is not reliable enough to decide the case. That is why I am sending it to a human reviewer rather than ruling for either of you, and why the $5.00 stays on hold, neither collected nor refunded, while that review is pending.

To the rider: the GPS trace from the driver's device is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(b). Inside the waiting window it has sampling gaps of 180 and 240 seconds (the limit is 120), it holds only four position fixes (the minimum is six), and it carries no rider track where POL-NS-04 needs rider position. It also puts no accuracy figure on any fix, so under POL-NS-02 no fix can establish arrival — but equally no fix can establish that the driver was elsewhere. That is absence of measurement, not proof of absence. Your argument that 'zero qualifying fixes' proves the driver never came does not succeed: the zero is produced by the trace's defects, so it can neither confirm the fee nor defeat it. Your alternative route, POL-NS-06, rests on the same trace and is undecided for the same reason. Your separate exoneration clause, POL-NS-04, does not apply: the chat log is complete and holds no message from you at all, so limb (a) fails, and in any event the driver placed an in-app call at 08:47:05 that went unanswered (limb (b)). POL-NS-05's false-arrival test is not engaged either — no fix places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at the marker — and POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) is not established, because the trace cannot show him stationary outside the radius but within 400 m. What POL-NS-06(i) would need — a present, populated traffic advisory — is absent (EV-ADVIS-00901-01, MISSING, weight 0.0), so no separate in-geofence intervals may be summed.

To the driver: your reliance on your own chat messages ('I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area') does not fill the gap. Those are your own account of arrival, and the arrival marker on the trip record was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so the marker and the trace are one carrier, not two. Where the GPS test admits no qualifying reading, an account offered in its place stands in for the test: it does not lift the confidence this ruling can carry, and the trace stays the only evidence of the deciding fact. Your entitlement under POL-NS-01 rests on limbs (b) and (c), both of which read that trace, and both are undecided rather than satisfied. The anti-farming check in POL-NS-07 cannot be run — no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d are both blank — so no abuse finding is made against you, but neither can compensation be confirmed.

On the money, the fare ledger is also impaired (weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD): the $5.00 charged does not reconcile with the $4.00 greater-of figure for a STANDARD zone and RYDE_X tier, which is a billing-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d). Because the charge itself is undecided, I note that defect for the reviewer rather than converting it into a figure here.

Because the only evidence for the deciding fact is the impaired trace (weight 0.6), POL-NS-08's closing sentence and POL-NS-09(e) apply: the ruling may not exceed a partial refund and the case goes to human review. My confidence is capped at the trace's 0.6, below the 0.70 floor, which is a second, independent ground for escalation under POL-NS-09(a). Escalation is terminal and replaces any money outcome.

Open question for the reviewer: can a validated copy of the driver's trace show he was within the pickup radius and held position for the full 300 seconds? That answer decides whether the fee stands, falls entirely, or is reduced to the $4.00 schedule figure.
